title: gamma-connectivity-chronology-and-comm-draft
content:
Quick notes / brain dump for Gamma outage (raw)

Context:
- Customer: Gamma Analytics (large enterprise). Running a dedicated cluster in us-west-2, model pinned to rwinf/model-7b-q4f.
- Incident triggered ~2026-03-09 18:02 UTC when customer reported 504s and streaming truncation for chat route /v1/chat/stream.
- Customer tenant id: tenant_gamma_42. Reported impact: 30% of requests erroring, higher tail latency.

Chronology (UTC timestamps are from our logs / agent events):
- 2026-03-09 17:58:12 - Autoscaler started rolling new nodes (scale-up event) after CPU spike on pool-dedicated-usw2-gamma. Scale request came from metric-scheduler, target pods +3.
- 2026-03-09 18:01:47 - First pod restart: serving-pod-7 reaped by kubelet (OOMKilled).
- 2026-03-09 18:02:03 - Customer support spike: Gamma support pinged via support@ and via account Slack.
- 2026-03-09 18:02:15 - Errors in proxy logs: 504 upstream read timeout for /v1/chat/stream; repeated.
- 2026-03-09 18:02:33 - Observed RPC errors in runtime logs: ERROR: rpc: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing
- 2026-03-09 18:03:10 - KV cache miss rate increases from 12% to 78% for model-7b-q4f, correlated with the restart churn.
- 2026-03-09 18:05:00 - Short-term mitigation: pin traffic to warm pods only (route rewrite to pool warm-usw2-gamma). Partial recovery in success rate to ~85%.
- 2026-03-09 18:12:00 - Observed repeated 502s from model process OOM logs while trying to allocate 2.8GB for kv cache.

Commands tried (notes + outputs paraphrased):
- kubectl get pods -n dedicated-gamma -o wide --show-labels
  -> found 3 pods in CrashLoopBackOff, restartCount 4/5
- kubectl logs serving-pod-7 -n dedicated-gamma --previous
  -> snippet: "model_worker[pid 1123] ERROR allocating KV cache: cannot mmap: Out of memory"
- curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' 'https://api.redwood.test/v1/health?tenant=tenant_gamma_42'
  -> connection reset occasionally, large TTFB on some nodes
- tail -n 500 /var/log/instances/serving-runtime.log | grep -E 'transport is closing|Unavailable|OOM'
  -> multiple segments matching transport is closing, then pod restart events
- checked autoscaler logs: scale event triggered by sustained cpu > 85% for 3 min; but pods scheduled to new machines that didn't have nv_cache warmed, so heavy cold cache load.

Error snippets captured:
- model_worker: ERROR allocating KV cache: cannot mmap: Out of memory
- runtime: ERROR: rpc: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing
- nginx: 504 upstream read timeout while reading response header from upstream
- kubelet: Pod "serving-pod-7" was killed due to memory pressure

Initial hypotheses (ranked):
1) Memory pressure combined with autoscaler churn caused repeated pod restarts which invalidated KV caches, causing heavy recomputation and memory allocations leading to further OOMs. Warm/cold mismatch across capacity caused cascading failures.
2) A regression in our memory accounting after deploy 2026-03-08 (minor runtime change) reduced reported available memory for model_worker leading to lower allocation headroom. Need to check PRs.
3) Network flakiness between proxy and runtime during node boot (MTU/multicast) caused rpc connections to break and left requests hanging until timeout (504).
4) Customer workload pattern (long context histories) drove unexpectedly high KV cache usage; their tenant had an artifact in prompts that prevented prefix caching effectiveness.

Evidence supporting #1:
- KV cache miss spike coincident with restart churn timestamp.
- OOM logs originating in model_worker when attempting to allocate 2.x-3.x GB for cache after restart.
- Partial recovery after manually directing traffic to already-warmed pods (reduced miss rate).

Evidence for #2:
- Recent runtime deploy at 2026-03-08 22:14 UTC (deploy-id deploy-2026-03-08-22:14). Need to diff commit that touched memory accounting.

Actions taken so far:
- Rerouted Gamma to warm pool (temporary).
- Increased soft memory limit on the serving group for Gamma (manual).
- Added a short-term autoscaler cooldown (from 60s -> 300s) for pool-dedicated-usw2-gamma to prevent aggressive churn.
- Collected heap profiles from 2 pods and uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/gamma/heap-2026-03-09-18.tgz

Next steps (TODO):
- [ ] Correlate deploy-2026-03-08 diff with memory accounting changes (assign: Marcus).
- [ ] Run reproduction with synthetic Gamma-ish workload in staging with same model and context lengths (assign: Lena).
- [ ] Add more detailed metrics around KV allocations and prefetch failure reasons. (assign: Priya)
- [ ] Customer comms: draft and send initial incident note with root-cause narrative and mitigation plan (draft below).
- [ ] Evaluate whether we owe a credit for 4 hours of degraded service. Ops to calculate exposure.

Draft internal -> customer message (rough):
Subject: Quick update on service disruption affecting Gamma on 2026-03-09
Hi Team Gamma,
We’re sorry for the disruption you experienced earlier today. Initial investigation shows a combination of memory pressure and autoscaler churn in your dedicated cluster that caused repeated pod restarts and invalidation of warm caches. This resulted in increased latency and a subset of requests timing out.
What we did immediately:
- Rerouted traffic to warmed instances to restore stability.
- Temporarily increased memory headroom and slowed autoscaling to reduce churn.

What we are doing next:
- Full postmortem to confirm root cause; initial focus is on a recent runtime change and cache allocation behavior.
- Hardening: longer autoscaler cooldown for dedicated pools, better pre-warm heuristics, and improved memory accounting.

We will follow up by EOD with a full timeline and a proposed compensation if SLA thresholds were breached. If you can share any request IDs that failed on your side, that will help validate what was returned.

Apologies again — we know this is disruptive.
Best,
Priya (on behalf of SRE + Runtime)

Notes to self / messy:
- check PR list: runtime/allocations, model-cache-evict in last week.
- confirm whether pod boot images include new 32-bit mem allocator flag.
- verify kernel dmesg for node where pod was OOMKilled.
- follow up with infra to see if the node had maintenance events around 17:55 UTC.

Slack threads: link above; create a channel gamma-incident-2026-03-09 if not already created.

End of raw notes. Keep this as a working scratch - will clean up and copy to shared_drives/customer-success/gamma when ready.
